key_insight: Multi-agent systems help when bounded inter-agent communication compresses redundant context without discarding too much task-relevant information, making the design an information bottleneck trade-off.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM systems, this means agent splitting and message budgets should be tuned to model strength and task structure rather than assumed to always improve performance.
method: Frames SAS vs. MAS through an information bottleneck perspective.
Shows that with unlimited relay bandwidth, a MAS can simulate any SAS by passing full context.
Introduces an effective bottleneck parameter (β) to capture the trade-off between context reduction and information loss.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the theory with 18 controlled experiments across five benchmarks and three model scales.
watch_item: If relay messages are too compressed, performance can drop below a single-agent baseline, especially for stronger models.
paper_title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
